title: Sexual Health and Gender-Based Violence
summary: Responsible decisions about sexuality, contraception and STI prevention, gender roles and stereotypes, gender-based violence, the law, and where survivors can get help.

notes.text: Decisions about relationships and sex affect your health, education and future. **Delaying** sexual activity (abstinence) is the safest choice for young teenagers. Anyone who is sexually active should use **condoms** every time to reduce the risk of HIV and other STIs, and a reliable contraceptive to prevent pregnancy.

rows: Yes, if used correctly every time
Can prevent pregnancy if taken soon after unprotected sex

notes.text: Youth-friendly clinics provide free, **confidential** services: HIV testing, contraception and treatment of STIs. In South Africa, children aged 12 and older can consent to an HIV test themselves.

**Gender roles** are society's expectations of how men and women should behave. Stereotypes such as 'boys don't cry' or 'girls must do the cooking' limit people's choices and can contribute to unequal power and violence.
Violence directed at a person because of their gender, or that affects one gender more than others. Most GBV in South Africa is committed by men against women and girls, but anyone can be a victim.

rows: Rape, unwanted touching, forcing someone to watch sexual images
Insults, threats, humiliation, controlling who someone sees
Taking someone's money, preventing them from working
Sharing private images without consent, tracking someone's phone, online harassment

notes.label: The law
notes.text: The **Domestic Violence Act** lets victims apply for a **protection order** at a magistrate's court. Sexual offences are crimes under the **Sexual Offences Act**. Sharing intimate images of someone without consent is a crime. Abuse is **never** the victim's fault.

items: Police (SAPS): 10111; Thuthuzela Care Centres at hospitals support rape survivors.
Tell a trusted adult, teacher or counsellor.
Challenge harmful gender stereotypes and jokes.
Build relationships based on equality and respect.

questions.prompt: Suggest THREE ways young people can help to prevent gender-based violence.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): challenge stereotypes; respect consent; report abuse; support survivors; build equal relationships; speak out

questions.prompt: Name TWO services offered by youth-friendly clinics.

questions.prompt: Name TWO places where a survivor of GBV can get help.
